exposure: length of stay in the postpartum center
contact with RSV-B positive staff members
outcome: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) type B infection
respiratory symptoms with or without fever
cohort: The study included 59 neonates who stayed at a postpartum center between January 1, 2017, and February 3, 2017, as well as their parents and the center's staff members.
finding: Longer periods of stay in the postpartum center were identified as the only risk factor for neonates becoming infected with RSV-B during the outbreak (Relative Risk = 8.10).
